title: The War Between Flesh and Spirit — Galatians 5:17
paragraphs: The War Between Flesh and Spirit — Galatians 5:17
Galatians 5:17 is not describing a weak Christian.
It is describing a war-torn one.

“The flesh desires what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh…”
That means the conflict in you is not always proof God left you. Sometimes it is proof the Spirit is fighting for territory your flesh used to rule.

Before Christ, many people sin with ease. No struggle. No grief. No conviction. Just appetite.
But when the Holy Spirit moves in, the old cravings do not leave quietly. They kick. They seduce. They whisper. They demand their throne back.
And this is where many believers panic.

They think, “Why am I still battling this?”
Why do I still feel the pull?
Why does temptation still know my name?

Temptation is not the same as surrender.
Struggle is not the same as defeat.
And war is not the same as abandonment.

The flesh wants what feels good now.
The Spirit wants what leads to life forever.
The flesh says, “Feed me.”
The Spirit says, “Follow Me.”
One leads to chains dressed like freedom.
The other leads to the cross… and then resurrection.

So yes, the battle is real.
But so is the power of God.

You are not called to make peace with the flesh.
You are called to crucify it.
Not by willpower alone.
Not by pretending.
Not by hiding.
But by walking in the Spirit, repenting quickly, staying in the Word, and clinging to Jesus when your knees shake.

This is the Gospel:
Jesus did not come just to forgive the acts of the flesh.
He came to break its dominion.
He lived the holy life you could not live, died the death your sin deserved, and rose again so you would not have to stay a prisoner to your old nature.

So if you are fighting, do not lose heart.
Run to Christ, not from Him.
The war inside you is fierce, yes.
But grace is fiercer.
And the Spirit does not lose.
“Walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.” — Galatians 5:16
